check_description: This check verifies that `market_overview.tex` uses the exact regulatory housing labels from the MPI/NAWAC Animal Welfare (Layer Hens) Code of Welfare 2018, avoids non-regulatory / marketing / American synonyms for those housing systems, keeps marketing tiers separate from housing systems, and annotates the colony cohort's end-2027 retailer-led phase-out. Where a source provides only a producer-level cage-free aggregate (barn + free-range combined), the compliant representation labels it 'barn + free-range' with the undisclosed split noted; 'cage-free' must not itself appear as a housing-system category label and may appear only as retailer-pledge / shelf-status framing. The registered company name 'Henergy Cage Free' is a proper noun and never counts as a violation.
score_0_criteria: Any of: (a) free-range labelled with marketing tier name ('pasture-raised', 'organic', 'cage-free'); or (b) barn labelled with non-regulatory term ('aviary', 'litter system') or collapsed with free-range under 'cage-free'; or (c) colony labelled with non-regulatory term ('enriched cage' as primary label, 'conventional'); or (d) a marketing tier (pasture-raised / organic / omega-3) presented as a separate primary housing system alongside free-range / barn / colony; a 4th category at the same level; without distinguishing it as a tier within free-range; or (e) colony presented as a stable / persistent housing category with no end-2027 phase-out annotation, transition arrow, or callout tying it to the retailer-led Phase 2 deadline; even if the deadline appears elsewhere on the page, the colony category itself must visibly carry the transition context; or (f-failure) any forbidden substitution appears as a primary housing-system label; 'cage free' or 'cage-free' used in place of 'barn' / 'free-range' / 'colony' as the category label (acceptable only as the retailer-pledge / shelf-status framing); or 'cage-free' introduced as a legend / category label for an aggregated barn + free-range block (the compliant label is 'barn + free-range, split not disclosed'); or 'free range' written without hyphen as the system label; or 'caged' used as a standalone housing-system label replacing 'colony' or 'colony cage'; or 'enriched cage' used as the primary colony-system label in place of 'colony' / 'colony cage'.
score_1_criteria: All six pass: (a) 'free-range' (hyphenated) used for the free-range housing system; verbatim regulatory term from nz_free_range_info_sheet.pdf title 'UNDERSTANDING NEW ZEALAND FREE-RANGE EGG FARMING'; (b) 'barn' used for the barn housing system per nz_barn_info_sheet.pdf 'A barn egg is laid by a hen in an indoor barn environment that does not contain cages'; (c) 'colony' or 'colony cage' used for the colony housing system per nz_colony_info_sheet.pdf 'A colony cage is an enlarged, inside enclosure that can house up to 60 hens'; (d) marketing tiers (pasture-raised, organic, omega-3) not presented as separate primary housing systems alongside free-range / barn / colony; either omitted from primary segmentation, or shown clearly as tiers within free-range with explicit visual or textual distinction (per Vivian Holst, #albatross-deal 2026-05-05 ts 1778002200: 'MPI's four housing systems are the primary cut (free-range, barn, colony, conventional cage). Pasture-raised, organic, and omega-3 are marketing tiers - they sit on top of free-range housing, not alongside it. Don't present them as separate primary housing systems in the deck. If we need to surface the premium dynamics, show them as sub-tiers within free-range with a clear visual or textual distinction. The four MPI labels are the structural taxonomy.'); (e) colony cohort annotated with end-2027 retailer-led Phase 2 phase-out context per Calthorpe Part 1 [00:07:31] 'The supermarket pledges to be cage-free by end of 2027 - both Foodstuffs and Woolworths NZ have committed publicly - have driven a lot of conversion ahead of the deadline' (annotation on colony category, transition arrow to barn / free-range with end-2027 deadline, or callout tying colony to Foodstuffs + Woolworths NZ end-2027 commitments); and (f) none of the following forbidden non-regulatory / marketing / American substitutions appear in `market_overview.tex` as housing-system labels on the page: 'cage free' or 'cage-free' used as a primary housing-system label (acceptable only as retailer-pledge / shelf-status framing such as 'cage-free shelf by end-2027'); where sources give only producer-level cage-free aggregates (Calthorpe Part 2 [00:32:10], e.g. 'Mainland is now closer to 85%', 'they're maybe 45-50% cage-free' (Heyden), 'Better Eggs is 65%. Zeagold is 70-75%.'), an aggregate block labelled 'barn + free-range (split not disclosed)' passes while a legend or category labelled 'cage-free' fails; the company name 'Henergy Cage Free' never counts; 'free range' written without hyphen as the system label; 'caged' as a standalone housing-system label; 'enriched cage' used as the primary system label in place of 'colony' or 'colony cage'. check_description:
This check verifies that `market_overview.tex` (and the compiled `market_overview.pdf`) complies with two firm-wide Halberd conventions: (a) the no-recommendation rule, and (b) US English spelling.

The deliverable must verify all of:
(a) No explicit invest / pass / continue-diligence recommendation language and no thesis-pillar framing in the title, intro, captions, or annotations. The rule is firm-wide per standards Section 9 and IC pre-read template Section 4 Hard Rules; both sources prohibit a recommendation position in any preliminary deliverable.
(b) US English spelling throughout the .tex source and the rendered .pdf body text (caption text, axis labels, intro sentence, TikZ annotations). Halberd is a US private-equity firm; US English is the implicit firm-wide convention. Any single instance of British / Commonwealth spelling fails this sub-criterion - e.g., 'realise' instead of 'realize', 'organise', 'colour', 'centre', 'programme', 'analyse', 'favour', 'behaviour', 'specialise'. Proper-noun spellings retain their canonical form (e.g., 'World Organisation for Animal Health' / WOAH, registered company names, official department names) and do not count as fails. LaTeX command names (e.g., `\colorbox`, `\centering`) are markup tokens, not authored prose, and do not count as fails either.

All sub-criteria must pass; failure on any one fails the check.

The four dimensions:
- (1) Source breadth and cross-referencing; distinct source count visibly cited in the depiction (footnotes, data labels, endnotes, in-place attributions), plus multi-source triangulation on the depiction's central numeric claims (producer shares, production-system mix, cage-free transition, retailer commitments) versus single-source reliance.
- (2) Data-quality caveats and framing; provenance / vintage flags on figures shown (e.g. FY25 actual vs FY26 forecast labelling; '2022-vintage' or 'as-of-2022 EPF baseline' tags on the stale-mix figures; 'as of' dates on time-sensitive data); sell-side framing tags on broker-sourced inputs (e.g. broker-asking 17-19% Aurora share flagged as sell-side, Calthorpe Part 2 18% flagged as the interview-refined working anchor); explicit handling of contradicting sources rather than silent averaging.
- (3) Explanation clarity and per-element analytical takeaway; legend / key / annotation readable; figures interpretable without external decoding (units, denominator, base-year stated in-line); the depiction's central analytical claim about market structure auditable from the on-page content alone. Distinct from P-01 which tests visual scannability (font size, layout, whitespace); this dimension tests whether the reader can audit the analytical claim from what's on the page.
- (4) Synthesis vs enumeration; the diagram tells the market structure story at a glance (producer concentration + channel structure + production-system transition arc) integrated into a coherent narrative, versus a flat collection of labelled boxes / numbers without prioritisation or causal / structural logic.

A stronger output addresses all four dimensions with concrete evidence. At least one observably stronger dimension with no material regression on the others determines the winner. Surface complexity (more nodes, denser annotations) does not satisfy a dimension unless substantive analytical depth is present.

- (3) Typographic and line-weight consistency. Title differentiated from section labels; node labels at consistent size; consistent font family across the page (no mixed serif / sans, no random typeface substitutions); arrow / box / divider line weights coherent. Use of preset TikZ styles (`\tikzset`) or `\newcommand` macros for a consistent visual vocabulary is preferred over inline ad-hoc styling that varies element-by-element.
- (4) Visual design discipline and aesthetic restraint. Restrained institutional colour palette (a defined set of 3-6 semantically named colours applied consistently - e.g. a primary navy / accent gold / neutral grey palette) beats arbitrary use of default TikZ pastel fills (`yellow!20`, `orange!20`, `red!20`, `brown!10` etc. picked ad hoc by what looks 'fine'). Colour assignments should be semantic and consistent across the page (e.g. the colour used for 'colony' in the production-system column should match the colour used for 'colony' wherever else it appears). Penalties: default TikZ pastels applied without a defined palette; >6 distinct fill colours without semantic justification; clashing colour combinations; over-decorated pages with splashy fills that obscure the structural content; under-decorated monochrome pages that miss hierarchy entirely.
- (5) Information hierarchy. Clear visual hierarchy across at least four typographic / colour strata: title > section / column header > primary node label > secondary annotation / footnote. Each stratum is distinguishable by some combination of size, weight, and colour. Pages where everything sits at similar visual weight (flat hierarchy) score lower than pages where the eye is led through the content by deliberate size / weight / colour contrast.
- (6) Legend, key, and annotation completeness. Colour coding, fill / hatch patterns, and arrow conventions explained via a legible legend or in-place key; annotations carry units / sources / dates where required. Footnote formatting: where footnotes are used, they are formatted at the bottom of the page (not floating mid-page), set at a footnote-appropriate size smaller than body text (e.g. `\footnotesize` or smaller), do not overlap the diagram body or page edge, and footnote numbering / markers match the in-diagram superscripts / markers exactly.
- (7) Compilation-render fidelity. The submitted `.tex` recompiles to a PDF that is visually identical to the submitted `.pdf` (no missing TikZ libraries, no font fallbacks producing different glyphs, no silent diagram-component drops). A-02 gates clean compilation as a binary; this dimension judges fidelity-of-match between source and submitted render.
score_0_criteria: Output B is observably more polished across the same seven dimensions (or strictly stronger on at least one with no regression). Visual judgements must be supportable from the rendered PDF; surface density is not polish. Ties on a dimension do not count toward either side. Overlapping shapes (nodes, boxes, or containers physically overlapping each other on the rendered page) is a near-automatic loss on dim (1) for the offending output, regardless of other spacing strengths. Arrows / lines / connectors that cross through node bodies or text labels at non-endpoint moments lose on dim (1). Text or elements clipped or bleeding off the page edge lose on dim (2). Mixed font families (e.g. serif title with sans body, or random typeface substitutions) or inconsistent label sizing lose on dim (3). Default TikZ pastel fills (`yellow!20`, `orange!20`, `red!20`, `brown!10`) used as the primary palette without a defined institutional colour scheme, or >6 distinct fill colours without semantic justification, or inconsistent semantic colour assignment across columns / rows lose on dim (4). Flat visual hierarchy where title, section headers, and body labels are indistinguishable in size / weight / colour loses on dim (5). Footnotes that float mid-page, sit at body-text size or larger, overlap the diagram body, or carry numbering mismatched with in-diagram superscripts lose on dim (6). Recompiled `.tex` producing a PDF that differs materially from the submitted PDF (missing libraries, font fallbacks, dropped components) loses on dim (7).
score_1_criteria: Output A is observably more polished across the seven dimensions: (1) tighter node and label spacing with no overlapping shapes (any shape-on-shape overlap is a near-automatic loss on this dim), comfortable margins, arrows / connectors not crossing through node bodies or labels other than at intended endpoints; (2) cleaner containment within shapes and page bounds (no clipping, no off-page bleed, connectors stay inside page bounds); (3) more consistent typography, font family, and line weights (title differentiated, consistent label sizing, coherent line weights), with preset TikZ styles or `\newcommand` macros preferred over inline ad-hoc styling; (4) more disciplined visual design (defined institutional colour palette of 3-6 semantically named colours, consistent semantic colour assignment, restrained decoration) beating default TikZ pastels applied ad hoc; (5) clearer information hierarchy across title > section / column header > primary label > secondary annotation, distinguishable by size / weight / colour; (6) more complete legend / key / annotation coverage with proper footnote formatting; (7) stronger compilation-render fidelity (recompiled PDF matches the submitted PDF without missing libraries, font fallbacks, or dropped components). check_description:
Pairwise: which `market_model.xlsx` is the more polished, professional Excel market-sizing workbook across four XLSX-specific presentation dimensions?
Four dimensions:
- (1) Workbook integrity: no error values (#REF!, #DIV/0!, #VALUE!, #NAME?, #N/A) in any populated cell; the workbook opens in fresh Excel / LibreOffice without recalculation errors or broken cross-sheet references.
- (2) Tab organisation and naming: tabs follow a sensible logical sequence (e.g. historical -> forecast -> scenarios -> assumptions, or equivalent); no default 'Sheet1' / 'Sheet2' names; no empty or placeholder tabs.
- (3) Number formatting and column hygiene: NZ$M / USD / % / decimal places are consistent within columns; column widths are sufficient (no '###' truncation; no zero-width columns hiding content); merged-cell content does not overflow or overlap; headers are readable.
- (4) Cross-sheet linkage: scenario tabs and the assumptions tab are linked by formula references rather than copy-pasted values; flexing an assumption propagates to the dependent scenario / output cells.
A stronger output is more polished across the four dimensions. Surface size (more rows, more tabs) is not polish; broken formulas or error cells in either output are an automatic loss on the workbook-integrity dimension.

The deck must verify all of: (a) No explicit invest / pass / continue-diligence recommendation language and no thesis-pillar framing (one-sided promotion implicitly recommends invest). (b) Every dollar figure on the deck is presented in USD. NZD (or other local-currency) figures are permitted ONLY when paired with their USD equivalent on the same slide, and the USD conversion must use the rate from the FX_Rates_Forecast or FX_Rates_Historical tab of halberd_central_financial_assumptions.xlsx that matches the time period of the underlying figure (historical figures use the FY-aligned historical rate for the year of the figure; multi-year forward / DCF figures use the FY-aligned forecast rate per year). A single flat spot rate applied across multi-year forecasts is disallowed. Unsourced spot rates or training-data rates are disallowed. The applied rate(s) and source workbook must be documented (footnote, slide footer, or speaker note). For deliverables with no financial figures (b) is satisfied by default. (c) Distinct key-findings synthesis section with findings within the cap. (d) Findings carry a sentiment / direction signal so positive and negative findings are both surfaced. (e) Separate prioritised risk register with risks within the cap. (f) US English spelling throughout the deliverable (every slide title, body text, footnote, speaker note, chart label, table caption). Halberd is a US private-equity firm; US English is the implicit firm-wide convention. Any single instance of British / Commonwealth spelling fails this sub-criterion - e.g., 'realise' instead of 'realize', 'organise', 'colour', 'centre', 'programme', 'analyse', 'favour', 'behaviour', 'specialise'. Proper-noun spellings retain their canonical form (e.g., 'World Organisation for Animal Health' / WOAH, registered company names, official department names) and do not count as fails.

All sub-criteria must pass; the synthesis section absent entirely is an automatic fail.
score_0_criteria: Any of: (a) explicit invest / pass / continue-diligence recommendation present; or thesis-pillar framing present ('compelling opportunity', 'attractive asset', 'strong fit for the platform'); or (b) any one of: any NZD (or other local-currency) figure appears on the deck without its USD equivalent on the same slide; or USD figures are presented without documentation of the FX rate(s) and source workbook (no footnote / footer / speaker note naming halberd_central_financial_assumptions.xlsx or the FY-aligned rate); or an unsourced spot rate / training-data rate / external-source rate is applied where the central workbook rate was required; or a single flat spot rate is applied across a multi-year forecast (e.g., one USD/NZD rate used for FY2026 through FY2030 figures); or the rate applied does not match the time period of the underlying figure (e.g., an FY2025 historical figure converted at an FY2028 forecast rate, or a forward-year forecast figure converted at an historical rate); or (c) fewer than 3 or more than 5 findings in the synthesis section; or (d) findings are presented as a flat list with no sentiment / direction signal; or (e) no separate prioritised risk register (risks only embedded in narrative without a 3-5 prioritised register); or (f) any single instance of British or Commonwealth spelling in the deck's own prose (excluding proper nouns / registered org names) - e.g., realise, organise, colour, centre, programme, analyse, favour, behaviour, specialise, kilometre, defence, licence (when used as a verb); one instance is enough to fail. This check verifies that `target_assessment.pptx` addresses Aurora's electricity-cost exposure across three required elements: NZ industrial electricity inflation backdrop, Aurora's 2027-28 contract-renewal step-up, and Aurora's structural scale-leverage gap vs Mainland.

The deck must verify all three of: (a) NZ industrial electricity inflation backdrop named. (b) Aurora's 2027-28 contract-renewal cost step-up named specifically. (c) Aurora's structural scale-leverage gap vs Mainland named.

All three required; the deck must remain in analytical framing without recommendation language.
score_0_criteria: NZ industrial electricity inflation backdrop not named (deck does not establish a rising electricity cost environment); or Aurora's 2027-28 contract-renewal step-up risk not named specifically (e.g., generic 'energy costs may rise' framing without the 2027-28 contract trigger); or Aurora's scale-leverage gap vs Mainland on electricity / supplier negotiation not named (Aurora and Mainland treated as having equivalent positions on electricity cost).
score_1_criteria: All three: (a) NZ industrial electricity inflation backdrop named; acceptable: 17.8 c/kWh 2024 anchor, or 2025 +12% increase, or forward curve / projection of ~18-20% cumulative over CY2024-26, or directly equivalent NZ-industrial electricity inflation framing (Calthorpe Part 7 [00:14:48] anchor); and (b) Aurora's 2027-28 contract-renewal cost step-up named specifically; acceptable: '2027 contract expiry', 'end-2027 / 2028 tariff renewal', 'electricity step-up at Phase 2 conversion period', or directly equivalent wording placing the trigger in the 2027-28 window (Part 7 [00:17:18] anchor: 'expires in late 2027 - right as Phase 2 conversion ramps electricity load on the new barn footprint'); and (c) Aurora's scale-leverage gap vs Mainland on electricity / supplier negotiation named; acceptable: 'two-site footprint vs Mainland multi-site', 'less gentailer leverage than Mainland', 'cannot replicate Mainland cross-site bundle pricing', 'one tier down on input-cost leverage vs Mainland', 'structurally short on electricity-cost smoothing', or directly equivalent wording naming Aurora's structurally weaker position.
specific_file_locations: Calthorpe Part 7 [00:14:48]: 'NZ industrial electricity prices have run hot. Statistics NZ / MBIE track average industrial electricity at approximately 17.8 cents per kilowatt-hour in 2024. Through 2025 large-user prices rose approximately 12% on the back of low-hydro / dry-winter wholesale spikes, and the 2026 forward curve from the four major gentailers - Meridian, Contact, Mercury, Genesis - is pointing to another 5%+ rise. So a producer with a fully-renewed five-year tariff expects approximately 18-20% cumulative electricity inflation over CY2024-26. That's a 150-220 basis point margin headwind on the colony / barn production lines if pass-through doesn't catch up.' Part 7 [00:17:18]: 'Aurora's hedging position on electricity. Their two sites are on standard large-commercial gentailer tariffs - I understand from the broker conversation they renewed the bulk of their electricity contract in calendar 2024 at then-prevailing rates ... captured the pre-2025-spike price level for approximately three years of the contract. That's lucky timing. But it expires in late 2027 - right as Phase 2 conversion ramps electricity load on the new barn footprint - and at that point they'll re-tariff into the post-2025 cost level. So the deck should name electricity as a 2027-28 cost step-up risk, not a near-term one. Mainland sits differently because their Otago / Manawatu / Auckland multi-site spread gives them three separate gentailer relationships and they actively negotiate cross-site bundle pricing. Aurora doesn't have the scale leverage for that.' Halberd supplier exposure annex section 3 codifies the electricity exposure (Stats NZ / Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment 17.8 c/kWh 2024; +12% 2025; +5%+ 2026; Aurora 2024 contract expires late 2027 into post-2025 cost level).

1. narrative coherence; primer + three findings + three open questions per the firm-wide IC pre-read convention, with primer / findings / questions distinct and arranged in a coherent arc.
2. evidence anchoring; each finding and open question tied to a specific data point, source claim, or quantifiable gap rather than generic narrative or platitude. Open questions in particular must be deal-specific and quantifiable.
3. no-recommendation discipline; pure assessment with no invest / pass / continue-DD verdict, per the firm-wide rule.
4. primer pillar coverage + pacing; primer covers the three pillars (supply chain end-to-end; hen lifecycle / production economics; by-product economics) at briefing depth, paced cleanly across the runtime without rushing pillars or padding.
5. visual-narration synergy; supporting visuals in `briefing.mp4` reinforce the specific data points being narrated rather than redundantly transcribing the voice; visuals advance with narration; static title-card-only or talking-head-only deliverables lose this dimension.

Score 1 (A wins): A is stronger across the five dimensions, or strictly stronger on at least one with no regression. Score 0 (B wins): B is stronger on the same basis. Deliverables that drift outside an appropriate briefing length or contain a recommendation or omit any one of the three primer pillars at substantive depth or show only a static title card / talking-head with no supporting visuals incur an automatic loss on those respective dimensions.

score_1_criteria: Output A is stronger across the five dimensions, or strictly stronger on at least one with no regression on the others. Specifically: cleaner primer + 3 + 3 structure with primer addressing all three pillars at substantive depth; better evidence anchoring with named figures and sources for both findings and open questions (open questions are deal-specific and quantifiable); no recommendation issued; primer + findings + open questions paced cleanly across whatever runtime is chosen; visuals meaningfully reinforce specific data points across the runtime. The five dimensions:

2. subtitle-audio alignment; subtitle text verbatim to spoken narration (per firm-wide convention) with timestamps matching audio cadence consistently across the runtime.
3. subtitle timing / readability; cue lengths readable (~2-5 seconds per cue, ~7-10 words per line, two lines max), no text too long to read in time on-screen; cue rate sustained naturally across the longer runtime.
4. audio quality; clear narration with consistent volume, no clipping, no digital artefacts, consistent voice across full runtime (no audio dropouts or volume jumps between primer / findings / open questions sections).
5. pacing across runtime; primer / findings / open questions paced cleanly: primer doesn't drag without substantive payload; findings and open questions each receive adequate runtime; transitions between sections are clean (deliberate pause, transition phrase, or visual cue rather than abrupt cut).
